svg.text: ESP32 main board on the CircuitSetup Project Box Breadboard
Top (component side) view, oriented as the board is printed: row a at the top, column 1 on the right (screw-terminal end).
ESP32-DevKitC (38-pin) raised on two 19-pin female headers in rows b and i, USB toward column 30. Dashed parts go under it and are soldered first.

• Dry-fit first: the ESP32's pin rows are 0.9" apart, so its headers should drop into rows b and i (this board's centre gap is 0.3"). If they don't, stop: the layout must change.

• This board's rails are not mirror images: on the a side the inner rail is − and the outer +, on the j side the inner rail is + and the outer −. Both + rails carry 3V3 here; only 5V goes straight to the relay.
• Rail holes are drawn at their column; use the nearest hole in that column. Ignore the half-columns of extra rail holes, the centre-gap pads, and the screw terminal.
• Rows a and j sit under the edge of the raised ESP32; wires soldered there leave sideways under the module's edge.
• Fit the 2.4 GHz U.FL antenna to the WROOM-32U before first power-up: it has no antenna of its own.
• The relay shield, SSR and all mains wiring stay off this board, in the mains compartment.
